SMTO-EXE-0156 — That computer can't do this desktop action right now

GUID: e1929c8b-9eed-550d-b59b-62a891865bb2
Slug: ui-target-capability-missing
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO asked the Gateway's computer to work with an app on its screen, but that computer reported it can't see or control apps right now. Nothing was clicked or typed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure someone is signed in on the Gateway's computer and its desktop is showing, awake and unlocked. Desktop actions only work in a signed-in, visible desktop, not at a lock or sign-in screen.
  2. On a Linux computer, sign out and sign back in choosing an Xorg (X11) session instead of Wayland. This computer offered neither app control nor keyboard and mouse control, and an X11 session gives SMTO keyboard and mouse control.
  3. Ask SMTO in the conversation to check what desktop actions that computer supports right now, then try the step again. SMTO can read the Gateway's live status and tell you whether it can now see and control apps there.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the desktop step, or its status check shows it can now work with apps on that computer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway's computer; they may need to install the accessibility support the Gateway uses. Don't turn off that computer's security protections to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • UIService found the operation's capability tag missing while live readiness reported the desktop as unavailable without a more specific unavailable_reason (on Linux or Windows, neither accessibility automation nor native input was usable).

What this means

  • The service's live readiness response omitted the required capability and supplied no more specific unavailable reason, so it selected the target-capability fallback. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • The service's live readiness response omitted the required capability and supplied no more specific unavailable reason, so it selected the target-capability fallback.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected Gateway's current capability list and the exact operation family; do not infer a specific missing package from the fallback label.

How to fix it

  • Run ui.status on the selected Gateway; it reports available=false with no unavailable_reason. On Linux provide a working AT-SPI accessibility bus with the Python Atspi (gi) bindings, or an X11 session with the XTEST extension (Wayland has no input fallback); on Windows make sure UI Automation (comtypes) loads and the Gateway runs as the signed-in desktop user, then retry.
  • Inspect ui.status and restore the actual missing prerequisite or choose a supported authorized action.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect ui.status and a fresh scoped ui.snapshot on the selected Gateway. Correct the target or prerequisites before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended session advertises the required capability or the unsupported requirement is reported.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
